## What the model says

The three-parameter mixture model ([Bays et al., 2009](https://doi.org/10.1167/9.10.7)), as
implemented in the R package [bmm](https://venpopov.com/bmm/), adds one kind
of response to the two-parameter mixture: reporting a non-target item instead of the target, a swap
error. On a fraction `p_mem` of the trials the participant recalls the target, on a fraction `p_nt`
reports one of the $n - 1$ non-targets, each equally often, and on the remaining trials guesses. All
memory responses, to the target or to a non-target, share the precision `kappa`. A response to a
non-target is centred on that item's colour $\mu_j$, measured from the target's colour, so the
response error $x$ follows (index 1 is the target, $\text{vM}(x;\, \mu, \kappa)$ the von Mises density
with mean direction $\mu$ and precision $\kappa$):

$$
f(x) = p_\text{mem}\,\text{vM}(x;\, 0,\, \kappa)
+ \frac{p_\text{nt}}{n - 1} \sum_{j=2}^{n} \text{vM}(x;\, \mu_j,\, \kappa)
+ \frac{1 - p_\text{mem} - p_\text{nt}}{2\pi}
$$

The three weights are probabilities of exclusive kinds of response, so $p_\text{mem} + p_\text{nt}
\le 1$ and guessing gets what remains. The page keeps the two sliders inside that limit: each
slider's upper end is 1 minus the other value. In bmm's model formulas `p_mem` is called `thetat` and `p_nt` `thetant`, and bmm does not estimate the
probabilities directly: it estimates `thetat` and `thetant` and turns them into weights with a softmax in which guessing is the
reference with the value 0, so $p_\text{mem} = e^{\theta_t} / (1 + e^{\theta_t} + e^{\theta_{nt}})$,
$p_\text{nt} = e^{\theta_{nt}} / (1 + e^{\theta_t} + e^{\theta_{nt}})$ and the guessing weight is
$1 / (1 + e^{\theta_t} + e^{\theta_{nt}})$. This page uses the probabilities, the argument names of
`dmixture3p()`.

## The task

One trial is a colour reproduction with several items. The participant sees $n$ coloured items, one
is cued, and the participant chooses its colour on the wheel. The model needs the response error and
the colour of every non-target relative to the target, both in radians. The wheel shows the target at
the top and the non-targets at their colours. Drag a dot to move a colour, or click it and use the
arrow keys; Even colours spreads them evenly around the wheel again, as does a new set size. The
locations of the items and their distances from the cued item do not enter the model; that is the
difference to the [interference measurement model](imm.qmd) (IMM), which uses them.

## Explore

The density has a peak at the target (blue) and one at each non-target's colour (orange), on the
flat floor of guesses (grey). Move `p_nt` and watch weight shift between the non-target peaks and the floor
or the target peak, move `kappa` and all peaks get narrower together, and drag a colour to move its
peak. The bars under the density show the weights: M for memory (the target), numbers for the
non-targets, G for guessing.

`kappa` has bmm's normal(2, 1) prior on the log scale; its slider spans the prior mean ± 3 SD in log
units, and the number field shows $e^{-1} = 0.37$ to $e^{5} = 148$. `p_mem` and `p_nt` run from 0 to
1 with the limit above, which the sliders keep as you move them: each stops where the other leaves
no room. The starting values, kept by the dashed curve and the "start" bars, are
`p_mem` = `p_nt` = 0.33 and `kappa` = $e^{2} = 7.39$: with `thetat` and `thetant` at 0, the medians of
bmm's logistic(0, 1) priors, the three weights are 1/3 each, which the sliders' step of 0.01 rounds
to 0.33, so guessing starts at 0.34. Typed values outside the sliders' ranges are used as long as they are valid. Reset returns
everything to the starting values.

## Across task settings

Set size enters the likelihood of `mixture3p` as the number of non-target peaks, and the
non-targets' colours set where those peaks sit. The non-targets share `p_nt` equally: one of the
$n - 1$ non-targets gets $p_\text{nt} / (n - 1)$ (bmm adds $\log(1 / (n - 1))$ to `thetant` for each
non-target), so a larger set size gives more non-target peaks, each lower than before, while all
of them together keep `p_nt`, as the target keeps `p_mem` and guessing the rest. Set size 1,
which `mixture3p()` accepts, has no non-target: bmm sets every non-target term to $-100$, the softmax
renormalises, and `p_nt` is split between the target and guessing in proportion to their own weights
(at `thetat` = `thetant` = 0, 0.5 each instead of a third each). The set-size control on this page
runs from 2 to 8. The Across set size panel draws the weights against set size. <span id="mix3-across-now"></span>

## In bmm

```{=html}
<div class="ex-widget">
  <pre class="ex-code" id="mix3-code"></pre>
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" id="mix3-copy">Copy</button>
</div>
<script type="module" src="../js/pages/mixture3p.js"></script>
```

The code updates with the controls. `dmixture3p()` returns the density for one trial; `mu` holds the
colours in radians, the target first. `mixture3p()` defines the model for a data set in which each
row is a trial: `resp_error` is the response error, `nt_features` names the columns with the
non-targets' colours, and `set_size` is the number of items on the display. `bmf()` writes the formula
and `bmm()` estimates the parameters; `my_data` stands for your own data, and fitting runs Stan
through brms. In the formula bmm calls `p_mem` `thetat` and `p_nt` `thetant`. See the
[mixture models article](https://venpopov.com/bmm/articles/bmm_mixture_models.html) and the
reference pages for [`mixture3p()`](https://venpopov.com/bmm/reference/mixture3p.html) and
[`dmixture3p()`](https://venpopov.com/bmm/reference/mixture3p_dist.html).
